!117 = !{!"/app/example.hlsl", !"//==========================================================================//\0A// What to look for: this file has two dx.op.rawBufferStore.i32/f32 calls. The FIRST\0A// (asuint(int2(123, 123)), an explicitly int32-typed literal) is fine on every pane. The\0A// SECOND (asuint((123).xx), a bare unsuffixed integer literal swizzled to a vector) is\0A// where DXC's own literal-typing rules (in the pre-HLSL-2021 default language mode) keep\0A// the literal 64-bit through the swizzle, so the asuint bitcast is applied to a 64-bit\0A// value instead of the 32-bit value the DXIL op expects. Look for the exit code (5 =\0A// E_FAIL) and the \22error: validation errors\22 / \22Invalid record\22 (or, on this Linux build,\0A// \22Call parameter type does not match function signature!\22) text -- that is DXIL\0A// validation catching the malformed module the front end produced, not a clean compile.\0A// Compare the \22-HV 2021\22 pane (still fails) against the \22-HV 202x\22 pane (compiles clean):\0A// the officially released HLSL 2021 language mode does NOT fix this; only the newer,\0A// still-experimental \22202x\22 preview mode does.\0A//==========================================================================//\0A\0ARWByteAddressBuffer sb : register(u0);\0A[numthreads(1, 1, 1)]\0Avoid main() {\0A  sb.Store(0, asuint(int2(123, 123))); // Okay\0A  sb.Store(0, asuint((123).xx)); // Boom\0A}\0A"}
